concept.name: Observability-Driven Testing

relationships.description: Connects Observability-Driven Testing to contract testing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Observability-driven testing (ODT) instruments tests and production traffic with structured traces, logs, and metrics so assertions verify internal distributed execution paths rather than just final HTTP status codes. It bridges pre-merge integration suites and controlled production experiments like canary analysis and chaos engineering.
spark.keyTakeaway: Emit OpenTelemetry trace context (`traceparent`) from every integration and E2E test so failures link directly to the exact microservice span, SQL query, or async consumer that broke—and reuse those same SLO telemetry queries to gate production canaries.

concept.whyItMatters: Traditional assertions (`assert response.status_code == 200`) miss silent partial failures—like a dropped Kafka event, a cache stampede, or an N+1 query regression that doubles p99 latency. ODT turns rich telemetry into verifiable test assertions and extends verification into production safely.
whenToUse: Testing asynchronous, event-driven, or microservice architectures (Kafka/SQS pipelines, saga orchestrators) where final state is eventual and black-box HTTP checks are flaky.
Gating progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts, Flagger) using automated canary analysis against real latency, error, and saturation SLIs.
Validating resilience under fault injection (Chaos Mesh, Gremlin, Toxiproxy) by asserting that circuit breakers, retries, and fallbacks fire as instrumented.
whenNotToUse: Pure unit tests of deterministic in-memory business logic or math functions—telemetry instrumentation adds unnecessary setup overhead over fast unit assertions.
Teams lacking basic structured logging or distributed tracing in staging/prod; ODT requires consistent OpenTelemetry context propagation first.
Replacing contract testing (Pact) or static type checking; ODT verifies runtime behavior, not compile-time schema compatibility.
keyPoints: Propagate W3C `traceparent` headers from test runners (Playwright, pytest, JUnit) into backend services and message brokers so each test run produces one unified distributed trace.
Assert on trace spans and structured events (e.g., `assert span('payment.charge').attributes['retry_count'] == 0` or `db.query_count <= 5`) using tools like Tracetest or Malabi.
Separate **synthetic test traffic** (`baggage: test_run_id=...`) from real user SLIs so load/chaos tests do not pollute production error budgets.
Use feature flags + dynamic telemetry sampling (100% head/tail sampling for `test_run_id` headers) to capture full forensic traces on flaky or failing tests.
Extend ODT to production via **Testing in Production**: shadow traffic, dark launches, and automated canary rollbacks driven by Prometheus/Datadog/Honeycomb queries.

examples.title: Catching Silent N+1 Queries in CI with Trace-Based Assertions
examples.scenario: An e-commerce checkout API passed all functional integration tests (`201 Created`), yet every deploy risked introducing ORM lazy-loading regressions that spiked RDS CPU in production.
examples.outcome: Adding Tracetest assertions on the CI OpenTelemetry trace (`span[db.system=postgresql].count <= 6` and `duration < 45ms` for a 5-item cart) caught two N+1 regressions before merge without writing brittle SQL mock assertions.

examples.title: Automated Canary Gating with Argo Rollouts & Prometheus
examples.scenario: A search ranking service deployed 6 times daily; manual dashboard watching during 10% canaries missed a 2x tail-latency regression on cold cache keys.
examples.outcome: Wiring an Argo Rollouts `AnalysisTemplate` to query `histogram_quantile(0.99, ...)` and `5xx` error rates every 60s for 10 minutes automatically aborted bad rollouts within 3 minutes and linked the failing `trace_id` to Slack.

tradeOffs.factor: Trace-Based Assertions vs. Mocked Unit Tests
tradeOffs.pro: Tests real serialization, network headers, SQL plans, and async broker handoffs with zero mock drift.
tradeOffs.con: Slower execution (seconds vs. milliseconds) and requires an ephemeral OTel collector/backend (Jaeger, Tempo, or Honeycomb) in CI.

tradeOffs.factor: 100% Test Trace Capture vs. Storage Cost
tradeOffs.pro: Tail-based or header-triggered sampling (`test_run_id` present) guarantees zero missing spans when debugging a rare race condition.
tradeOffs.con: High-volume load tests with 100% tracing enabled can overwhelm OTel Collector memory or blow through vendor ingest quotas.

tradeOffs.factor: Testing in Production (Canaries) vs. Staging-Only Gates
tradeOffs.pro: Exposes real data distributions, DNS/TLS quirks, and third-party API latency that staging mocks never reproduce.
tradeOffs.con: Requires strict blast-radius controls (1%–5% traffic splits, synthetic test accounts, idempotent mutations) to protect real users.

failureModes.name: Broken Context Propagation Across Async Queues
failureModes.description: A Kafka or SQS producer omits `traceparent` in message headers, splitting one test trace into disconnected orphan traces and causing trace assertions to time out.
failureModes.mitigation: Use OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for Kafka/SQS/RabbitMQ headers and add a CI smoke check verifying parent-child `trace_id` continuity across async boundaries.

failureModes.name: Async Span Flush Race in Short-Lived Tests
failureModes.description: The test runner queries Jaeger/Tempo 100ms after the HTTP response returns, before the service's `BatchSpanProcessor` (default 5s delay) flushes spans.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure shorter flush intervals (`OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=500`) in test environments and poll the trace backend with exponential backoff up to 5–10 seconds.

failureModes.name: Test Traffic Polluting Production SLOs
failureModes.description: Synthetic E2E or chaos tests running against production trigger false-positive PagerDuty alerts and burn real customer error budgets.
failureModes.mitigation: Tag all synthetic traffic with `synthetic=true` in OTel baggage/attributes and filter `synthetic!="true"` out of all SLO burn-rate and alerting queries.

failureModes.name: Brittle Span Name Coupling
failureModes.description: Tests assert on exact internal function names or auto-generated span strings that break whenever a developer refactors a private helper.
failureModes.mitigation: Assert on stable OpenTelemetry semantic conventions (`http.status_code`, `db.operation`, `messaging.destination.name`) and explicit domain span names.

commonMistakes: Relying on `sleep(5)` in async tests instead of polling the trace/telemetry backend for the expected completion span.
Allowing the OpenTelemetry `BatchSpanProcessor` to drop spans silently under CI load without checking `otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans`.
Running chaos experiments without defining steady-state telemetry hypotheses (e.g., error rate < 0.5%, fallback hit rate > 99%) beforehand.
Instrumenting only HTTP ingress and ignoring downstream database, Redis, and third-party webhook spans.
Leaving 100% debug trace sampling enabled in load tests, crashing the OTel Collector with OOMKills.

sections.content:
## The idea

Traditional testing treats a distributed system like a black box: send an input, wait, and assert on the output. When a 6-service workflow fails—or succeeds slowly because of 40 redundant database queries—black-box tests either miss the regression entirely or fail with an unhelpful timeout.

**Observability-driven testing (ODT)** flips the model to white-box runtime verification. It uses the same **OpenTelemetry (OTel)** traces, structured logs, and metrics that power production debugging as **first-class test assertions** in CI and **automated quality gates** during progressive production rollouts.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider an async order-fulfillment flow (`POST /orders` -> Order Service -> Kafka `orders.created` -> Inventory Service -> Postgres) tested in CI with Tracetest and OpenTelemetry:

1. **Inject Trace Context**: The test runner generates `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01` (sampling flag `01` forces 100% capture) and sends `POST /orders`.
2. **Propagate Across Boundaries**: Order Service records an HTTP server span, writes to Postgres, and injects `traceparent` into the Kafka message headers before returning `202 Accepted`.
3. **Async Worker Execution**: Inventory Service consumes the Kafka event, extracts `traceparent` as its parent span, reserves stock in Postgres, and emits its own spans to the OTel Collector.
4. **Query & Assert on Telemetry**: After `202 Accepted`, the test runner polls Tempo/Jaeger by `trace_id` (`4bf92f35...`). It asserts: (a) `POST /orders` status == `202`, (b) Kafka consumer span `inventory.reserve` completed with `status.code == OK`, (c) total `db.system=postgresql` spans <= 4, and (d) end-to-end trace duration < 250ms.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Span assertions, chaos verification, and canary analysis
sections.content:
## Span assertions, chaos verification, and canary analysis

ODT spans three operational stages:

1. **CI Trace Assertions**: Validate internal invariants—no unindexed full-table scans (`db.rows_examined`), zero unexpected retries, and exact event fan-out counts.
2. **Chaos & Fault-Injection Verification**: Tools like Chaos Mesh or Toxiproxy inject 300ms network latency or kill a Redis pod while tests assert that the `resilience4j.circuitbreaker` span transitions to `OPEN` and serves cached fallback data within 50ms.
3. **Progressive Production Verification**: Argo Rollouts or Flagger shifts 5% of live traffic to the canary and runs PromQL/Honeycomb queries comparing canary vs. baseline `http_server_duration_p99` and `5xx` rate, auto-promoting or rolling back without human intervention.

## Traditional testing vs. observability-driven testing

| Dimension | Traditional Black-Box Testing | Observability-Driven Testing (ODT) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Signal** | HTTP response body & status code | Full OTel trace tree, span attributes, & SLIs |
| **Async / Event Workflows** | Fragile `sleep()` or DB polling loops | Deterministic polling on downstream consumer spans |
| **Performance Regressions** | Caught late in separate load tests | Caught per-PR via `db.query_count` & span duration |
| **Failure Triage** | Grep container logs to guess cause | Direct deep-link to failing `trace_id` & exact span |
| **Production Coverage** | Stops at pre-prod staging | Extends to automated canary & chaos verification |

## Failure modes

**1. High-Cardinality Label Explosion from Test Runs**: Putting a unique `test_run_id` into a Prometheus metric label (`http_requests_total{test_run_id="..."}`) creates millions of time series and OOMs Prometheus. Always put `test_run_id` in **trace attributes and structured logs**, never in Prometheus metric labels.

**2. Telemetry Pipeline Lag Causing Flaky CI**: If the CI OTel Collector buffers batches for 5–10 seconds, trace assertions fail intermittently. Use an in-memory or fast-flush collector config (`send_batch_size: 100`, `timeout: 200ms`) in CI.

**3. False Confidence from Unrepresentative Synthetic Data**: Canaries with low traffic (<10 req/min) lack statistical power for p99 comparisons; pair canary gating with synthetic probe traffic or minimum sample thresholds.

sections.eyebrow: 06 / Integrating ODT into CI/CD and production
sections.content:
## Integrating ODT into CI/CD and production

To adopt ODT incrementally without rewriting existing suites:

- **Week 1 (Context Propagation)**: Add OTel SDKs and pass `traceparent` from Playwright/API tests; print the Jaeger/Tempo trace URL on any test failure.
- **Week 2 (Invariant Assertions)**: Add 3–5 high-value trace assertions on critical checkout/auth flows (max DB queries, zero `ERROR` spans, required async consumer completion).
- **Week 3 (Canary Gating)**: Reuse those exact PromQL/OTel queries in Argo Rollouts `AnalysisTemplate` so pre-prod and prod share one source of truth.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Propagate W3C `traceparent` and `baggage` across HTTP, gRPC, and message brokers (Kafka/SQS).
- [ ] Force sampling (`sampled=1`) on CI and synthetic test requests; exclude `synthetic=true` from prod SLOs.
- [ ] Never attach unbounded `test_run_id` values to Prometheus metric labels (use trace/log attributes only).
- [ ] Tune CI `BatchSpanProcessor` flush delay to `<= 500ms` to avoid assertion race conditions.
- [ ] Assert on semantic attributes (`db.system`, `http.status_code`, `rpc.grpc.status_code`) rather than private function names.
- [ ] Gate production canaries with automated SLI queries (p99 latency, 5xx rate, saturation) for 5–15 minutes.

interviewProblems.title: Observability-Driven Testing
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Observability-Driven Testing. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Observability-driven testing (ODT) instruments tests and production traffic with structured traces, logs, and metrics so assertions verify internal distributed execution paths rather than just final HTTP status codes. It bridges pre-merge integration suites and controlled production experiments like canary analysis and chaos engineering.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: OTel Collector + Tempo applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Assertion / Canary Gate.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Assertion / Canary Gate experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Use OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for Kafka/SQS/RabbitMQ headers and add a CI smoke check verifying parent-child `trace_id` continuity across async boundaries.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Emit OpenTelemetry trace context (`traceparent`) from every integration and E2E test so failures link directly to the exact microservice span, SQL query, or async consumer that broke—and reuse those same SLO telemetry queries to gate production canaries.
Avoid trap: Relying on `sleep(5)` in async tests instead of polling the trace/telemetry backend for the expected completion span.
Avoid trap: Allowing the OpenTelemetry `BatchSpanProcessor` to drop spans silently under CI load without checking `otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans`.
When to reach for it: Testing asynchronous, event-driven, or microservice architectures (Kafka/SQS pipelines, saga orchestrators) where final state is eventual and black-box HTTP checks are flaky.
When to reach for it: Gating progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts, Flagger) using automated canary analysis against real latency, error, and saturation SLIs.

putItTogether.title: Putting Observability Driven Testing Together
putItTogether.summary: Emit OpenTelemetry trace context (`traceparent`) from every integration and E2E test so failures link directly to the exact microservice span, SQL query, or async consumer that broke—and reuse those same SLO telemetry queries to gate production canaries.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Observability Driven Testing before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Adding Tracetest assertions on the CI OpenTelemetry trace (`span[db.system=postgresql].count <= 6` and `duration < 45ms` for a 5-item cart) caught two N+1 regressions before merge without writing brittle SQL mock assertions.
